the drug delivery design is a key parameter in the development of taxanes and should be taken into account from the very early stage of preclinical studies to the clinical phase.
surfactant based formulations are not efficient in clinic due to the high variability in the plasma concentration and the poor pharmacokinetics profile.

the drug delivery technologies are not only important to improve the efficacy and safety, but they are also important to provide the rationale for the development of new drug delivery technologies.

(i) the pharmacokinetics of the drug in plasma is not only driven by the physicochemical properties of the formulation but also by the drug itself and its metabolism and (ii) a good correlation between the in vivo efficacy of a taxane drug delivery design and its physicochemical properties can be observed.

, in order to achieve a better understanding of the drug delivery design for intravascular injection, it is necessary to integrate physicochemistry, in vitro and in vivo pharmacokinetics and the pharmacodynamics of a drug formulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the drug delivery technologies are a powerful tool in the design of anticancer drugs.
the drug delivery design for the intravenous route should take into account the physicochemical properties of the drug and the carrier as well as their interactions.
the drug delivery design is not only a question of drug formulation but also of drug pharmacokinetics, biodistribution and pharmacodynamics.
